events.content: See tissue packet moved, Rachel sitting there. My options: 1) Say directly that packet was mine and ask for it back; 2) Offer to share if she needs seat; 3) If she refuses, find another seat. Prefer quick, practical, no drama. Plan: state the concrete problem first, then offer a face-saving compromise (share) if needed. Keep voice calm but firm, use short Singlish phrases so she understands I'm local.

Excuse me. You moved my tissue packet and sat here. I left it to chope this seat while I bought food. Can you please put it back so I can sit? If you need the table, no problem — we can share. Thank you.
Waiting to see her response.

He says I moved his tissue packet and left to chope the seat. I remember the table looked empty and the packet was unopened, so I moved it slightly and sat down — I thought it was abandoned. I don't like being treated as inconsiderate before I can explain myself, but I should stay calm. Plan: explain what I thought, ask whether he left it intentionally, then offer to put the packet back or share the table depending on what he wants.

Waiting for Mr Lim's response.

event.summary: Rachel moves a tissue packet from an otherwise empty table and sits down just as Mr Lim returns carrying his food.

evidence.category: Conflict claim (chope)
evidence.quote: You moved my tissue packet and sat here. I left it to chope this seat while I bought food.

evidence.category: Rachel explains she moved packet, unaware of chope
evidence.quote: I honestly didn't realise you left the tissue packet to chope the seat; the table looked empty and the packet was still sealed, so I moved it to the side and sat down because I thought no one was coming back.

evidence.category: Rachel offers to return seat / put packet back
evidence.quote: If you did intend to chope, I'm happy to put the packet back and give you the seat, or we can share the table if that's easier. Which would you prefer?

evidence.category: Mediator suggests sharing and offers quick resolution
evidence.quote: Maybe easiest is to share the table so nobody needs to move, or if you really prefer the seat, Rachel has offered to give it back. Which would you prefer, Mr Lim? If you want, Rachel can put the packet back now and we settle it quickly.

evidence.category: Secondary mediator concurs (sharing or return)
evidence.quote: Mr Lim — maybe easiest is to share the table so nobody needs to move. If you'd rather have the seat back, Rachel has offered to put the packet back, so it's your call.

evidence.category: Mr Lim reiterates chope and offers options (practical)
evidence.quote: I left the tissue packet to chope this seat. Rachel, you said you can put it back — if you don't mind, please put the packet back and I will sit. If you rather stay, okay we share the table. No need make big thing lah.

evidence.category: Rachel accepts and commits to put packet back (resolution)
evidence.quote: Alright Mr Lim — no problem, I'll put the tissue packet back now. Sorry for the confusion; the packet looked unopened and I genuinely thought the table was free. Please take the seat, and thank you for letting me know.

evidence.category: Mr Lim acknowledges and takes seat (outcome confirmed)
evidence.quote: Okay, thanks Arjun. Rachel, thanks for putting the packet back. No need make big thing — enjoy your lunch, everyone.

evidence.category: Rachel apologises / concedes (supports compromise)
evidence.quote: Thanks, Mr Lim — I appreciate it. Sorry again for the confusion earlier. Enjoy your lunch.

evidence.category: Nur Aisyah closes interaction (mediator closure)
evidence.quote: Thanks Rachel — I appreciate you being understanding. Mr Lim, please go ahead and take your seat. Rachel, no problem at all. All good now, enjoy your lunch everyone.
